headline: Monitor Medano Creek Forecasts and Pinon Flats Availability
reservation: A standard park entry does not require a timed reservation, but the Pinon Flats Campground requires booking through official federal systems. Peak weekends during spring creek flow see extreme demand for local lodging. Always verify current entry policies and backcountry permit needs on the official NPS site before travel.

days.title: High Dunes and Hydrology

stops.name: High Dune on the First Ridge
stops.detail: Ascend the most prominent front-range dune for panoramic views of the 30-square-mile dunefield and Sangre de Cristo Mountains.

stops.name: Medano Creek
stops.detail: Wade in the seasonal surge-flow waters at the dunes' base, typically peaking in late May or June depending on snowpack.

days.driving: Allow 60–90 minutes for the round trip from Alamosa; conditions vary by wind.
days.note: Sand surface temperatures can exceed 150°F (65°C) by midday; early starts are essential.

days.title: Forest Transitions and History

stops.name: Montville Nature Trail
stops.detail: Walk this shaded loop to see the site of a former 1880s settlement and enjoy views of the sand-to-mountain transition.

stops.name: Great Sand Dunes Visitor Center
stops.detail: View the park film and exhibits to understand the geologic forces of wind and water that formed the tallest dunes in North America.

days.driving: Local park roads are paved and short; allow 20 minutes between main sites.
days.note: Afternoon thunderstorms are common; move to a hard-topped vehicle if lightning threatens.

days.title: Foothills and Falls

stops.name: Zapata Falls
stops.detail: Located just outside the park boundary, this site offers a secluded waterfall view through a rocky crevice.

stops.name: Mosca Pass Trail
stops.detail: Follow an old wagon route through aspen and evergreen forests for a different perspective of the San Luis Valley.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes to reach the Zapata Falls trailhead; the access road is steep and gravel.
days.note: Reaching the base of Zapata Falls involves wading in very cold water over slippery rocks.

intel.title: Dunes Access Parking
intel.text: The main lot near Medano Creek fills rapidly during peak flow weekends in May and June. Arrive before 9 AM or consider visiting on a weekday to avoid congestion.

intel.title: Limited Cellular Service
intel.text: Signal is highly unreliable once you enter the park gates and non-existent in the dunefield. Download offline maps and park information in Alamosa before departing.

intel.title: San Luis Valley Supplies
intel.text: Alamosa serves as the primary hub for fuel, groceries, and sandboard rentals. Ensure your tank is sufficient for the return trip as services near the dunes are extremely limited.

intel.title: Surface Temperature Hazards
intel.text: Plan dune hiking for the first three hours of daylight to avoid heat exhaustion and blistering. In fall, budget time for rapidly dropping temperatures after the sun dips behind the mountains.

intel.title: Primitive Road Requirements
intel.text: Medano Pass Primitive Road requires high-clearance 4WD vehicles and involves deep sand and creek crossings. Rental car agreements often prohibit travel on this specific route.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental vehicle at San Luis Valley Regional Airport (ALS) and stop in Alamosa for a sandboard rental and water supplies before the 55-minute drive to Mosca-area lodging.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are fine for paved park roads, but an RV may have restricted turnarounds in smaller trailhead lots; check length limits for Pinon Flats.
plan.goldenHour: The summit of High Dune offers dramatic shadows at sunset, though hikers should carry headlamps for the descent as light fades quickly.
